```{r}

# ================================================================
# lmeEEG TUTORIAL — R IMPLEMENTATION
#
# Reference:
# https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jneumeth.2023.109991
#
# Pipeline:
# 1. Load EEG and experimental design
# 2. Fit LMMs and extract marginal EEG
# 3. Perform mass-univariate OLS
# 4. Generate observed TFCE maps
# 5. Perform constrained permutations
# 6. Calculate FWER-corrected p-values
# 7. Visualize and save results
#
# IMPORTANT:
# This is an R adaptation, not a numerically validated
# replacement for the original MATLAB MEX TFCE function.
# ================================================================


# ================================================================
# STEP 0: PACKAGES AND DATA
# ================================================================

packages <- c(
  "lme4",
  "R.matlab",
  "ggplot2"
)

missing_packages <- packages[
  !vapply(packages, requireNamespace,
          logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing_packages)
}

library(lme4)
library(R.matlab)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(123)

# -------- Load data --------

mat <- readMat("sEEG_all.mat")

sEEG_all <- mat$sEEG_all

# If times are stored in another MAT file,
# adjust this section.
if (!is.null(mat$sEEG_times)) {
  sEEG_times <- as.numeric(mat$sEEG_times)
} else {
  stop("sEEG_times not found. Load the time vector.")
}

sEEG_table <- read.csv("sEEG_table.csv")

sEEG_table$ID <- factor(sEEG_table$ID)
sEEG_table$Item <- factor(sEEG_table$Item)

sEEG_table$CON <- factor(
  sEEG_table$Condition,
  levels = c("A", "B")
)

n_chan <- dim(sEEG_all)[1]
n_time <- dim(sEEG_all)[2]
n_trials <- dim(sEEG_all)[3]

stopifnot(
  length(dim(sEEG_all)) == 3,
  nrow(sEEG_table) == n_trials,
  length(sEEG_times) == n_time,
  !anyNA(sEEG_all),
  !anyNA(sEEG_table[, c("ID", "Item", "CON")])
)

X <- model.matrix(
  ~ CON,
  data = sEEG_table
)

coef_names <- colnames(X)
n_coef <- ncol(X)

cat("Channels:", n_chan, "\n")
cat("Timepoints:", n_time, "\n")
cat("Trials:", n_trials, "\n")


# ================================================================
# STEP 1: MIXED-EFFECTS MODELS
# ================================================================

# MATLAB:
# EEG ~ CON + (1|ID) + (1|Item)
#
# Marginal EEG:
# fixed-effect prediction + conditional residuals

fit_marginal <- function(y, events) {

  dat <- data.frame(
    EEG = as.numeric(y),
    CON = events$CON,
    ID = events$ID,
    Item = events$Item
  )

  model <- lmer(
    EEG ~ CON + (1 | ID) + (1 | Item),
    data = dat,
    REML = TRUE,
    control = lmerControl(
      check.conv.singular = "ignore"
    )
  )

  fixed_prediction <- predict(
    model,
    re.form = NA
  )

  marginal <- fixed_prediction +
    residuals(model)

  return(as.numeric(marginal))
}

mEEG <- array(
  NA_real_,
  dim = dim(sEEG_all)
)

cat("Fitting mixed-effects models...\n")

for (ch in seq_len(n_chan)) {

  for (tp in seq_len(n_time)) {

    y <- sEEG_all[ch, tp, ]

    mEEG[ch, tp, ] <- fit_marginal(
      y,
      sEEG_table
    )
  }

  cat("Completed channel", ch, "/", n_chan, "\n")
}

cat("Marginal EEG extraction completed.\n")


# ================================================================
# STEP 2: MASS-UNIVARIATE LINEAR REGRESSION
# ================================================================

mass_ols <- function(Y, X) {

  Y <- as.matrix(Y)
  X <- as.matrix(X)

  if (nrow(Y) != nrow(X)) {
    stop("Y and X must have the same number of rows.")
  }

  if (anyNA(Y) || anyNA(X)) {
    stop("Missing values are not supported.")
  }

  n <- nrow(X)
  p <- ncol(X)

  qrX <- qr(X)

  if (qrX$rank != p || n <= p) {
    stop("Invalid or rank-deficient design matrix.")
  }

  beta <- qr.coef(qrX, Y)

  residual <- Y - X %*% beta

  sigma2 <- colSums(residual^2) / (n - p)

  XtX_inv <- chol2inv(chol(crossprod(X)))

  se <- sqrt(
    outer(diag(XtX_inv), sigma2)
  )

  tval <- beta / se

  list(
    t = tval,
    beta = beta,
    se = se
  )
}

# Trials x channel-timepoint matrix
Y <- t(matrix(
  mEEG,
  nrow = n_chan * n_time,
  ncol = n_trials
))

fit <- mass_ols(Y, X)

t_obs <- array(
  t(fit$t),
  dim = c(n_chan, n_time, n_coef)
)

betas <- array(
  t(fit$beta),
  dim = c(n_chan, n_time, n_coef)
)

se <- array(
  t(fit$se),
  dim = c(n_chan, n_time, n_coef)
)

dimnames(t_obs)[[3]] <- coef_names
dimnames(betas)[[3]] <- coef_names
dimnames(se)[[3]] <- coef_names

cat("Mass-univariate regression completed.\n")


# ================================================================
# STEP 3: CHANNEL NEIGHBORHOODS
# ================================================================

# Export ChN from MATLAB:
#
# ChN = ept_ChN2(chanlocs);
# writematrix(ChN, "channel_neighbors.csv");
#
# This script assumes ChN is a symmetric binary
# channel x channel adjacency matrix.

ChN <- as.matrix(
  read.csv(
    "channel_neighbors.csv",
    header = FALSE
  )
)

storage.mode(ChN) <- "numeric"

stopifnot(
  nrow(ChN) == n_chan,
  ncol(ChN) == n_chan,
  all(is.finite(ChN)),
  all(ChN == t(ChN)),
  all(ChN %in% c(0, 1))
)

diag(ChN) <- 0


# ================================================================
# STEP 4: CONNECTED COMPONENTS FOR TFCE
# ================================================================

find_components <- function(mask, adjacency) {

  nc <- nrow(mask)
  nt <- ncol(mask)

  visited <- matrix(FALSE, nc, nt)
  components <- list()

  for (ch in seq_len(nc)) {
    for (tp in seq_len(nt)) {

      if (!mask[ch, tp] || visited[ch, tp]) {
        next
      }

      start <- (tp - 1L) * nc + ch

      queue <- start
      visited[ch, tp] <- TRUE

      component <- integer(0)
      head <- 1L

      while (head <= length(queue)) {

        idx <- queue[head]
        head <- head + 1L

        component <- c(component, idx)

        c0 <- ((idx - 1L) %% nc) + 1L
        t0 <- ((idx - 1L) %/% nc) + 1L

        spatial <- which(
          adjacency[c0, ] != 0
        )

        neighbors <- (
          (t0 - 1L) * nc + spatial
        )

        if (t0 > 1L) {
          neighbors <- c(
            neighbors,
            idx - nc
          )
        }

        if (t0 < nt) {
          neighbors <- c(
            neighbors,
            idx + nc
          )
        }

        for (nb in neighbors) {

          cn <- ((nb - 1L) %% nc) + 1L
          tn <- ((nb - 1L) %/% nc) + 1L

          if (
            mask[cn, tn] &&
            !visited[cn, tn]
          ) {

            visited[cn, tn] <- TRUE
            queue <- c(queue, nb)
          }
        }
      }

      components[[length(components) + 1L]] <-
        component
    }
  }

  return(components)
}


# ================================================================
# STEP 5: TFCE TRANSFORMATION
# ================================================================

# TFCE parameters:
# E = 0.66
# H = 2
#
# Positive and negative clusters are treated separately.
#
# This is a numerical approximation and has not been
# validated against ept_mex_TFCE2D.

tfce_2d <- function(
    stat,
    adjacency,
    E = 0.66,
    H = 2,
    dh = 0.1
) {

  stopifnot(
    is.matrix(stat),
    all(is.finite(stat)),
    nrow(adjacency) == nrow(stat),
    ncol(adjacency) == nrow(stat),
    dh > 0
  )

  transform_side <- function(x) {

    output <- matrix(
      0,
      nrow(x),
      ncol(x)
    )

    max_h <- max(x)

    if (max_h <= 0) {
      return(output)
    }

    # Midpoint numerical integration with
    # a potentially shorter final interval.
    edges <- seq(0, max_h, by = dh)

    if (tail(edges, 1) < max_h) {
      edges <- c(edges, max_h)
    }

    for (k in seq_len(length(edges) - 1L)) {

      width <- edges[k + 1L] - edges[k]
      h <- (edges[k] + edges[k + 1L]) / 2

      mask <- x >= h

      components <- find_components(
        mask,
        adjacency
      )

      for (component in components) {

        extent <- length(component)

        output[component] <-
          output[component] +
          extent^E * h^H * width
      }
    }

    output
  }

  positive <- transform_side(
    pmax(stat, 0)
  )

  negative <- transform_side(
    pmax(-stat, 0)
  )

  return(positive - negative)
}


# ================================================================
# STEP 6: OBSERVED TFCE MAPS
# ================================================================

tfce_obs <- array(
  NA_real_,
  dim = dim(t_obs),
  dimnames = dimnames(t_obs)
)

for (j in 2:n_coef) {

  tfce_obs[, , j] <- tfce_2d(
    t_obs[, , j],
    adjacency = ChN,
    E = 0.66,
    H = 2,
    dh = 0.1
  )
}

cat("Observed TFCE maps computed.\n")


# ================================================================
# STEP 7: PERMUTATION MATRIX
# ================================================================

# For a fully crossed subject-item design,
# use the original lmeEEG permutation indices.
#
# MATLAB:
#
# rperms = lmeEEG_permutations2(nperms, ID, Item);
# writematrix(rperms, "rperms.csv");
#
# This avoids substituting unrestricted permutations.

rperms <- as.matrix(
  read.csv(
    "rperms.csv",
    header = FALSE
  )
)

storage.mode(rperms) <- "integer"

nperms <- ncol(rperms)

stopifnot(
  nrow(rperms) == n_trials,
  all(rperms >= 1L),
  all(rperms <= n_trials)
)

valid_perms <- apply(
  rperms,
  2,
  function(idx) {
    identical(
      sort(idx),
      seq_len(n_trials)
    )
  }
)

stopifnot(all(valid_perms))


# ================================================================
# STEP 8: PERMUTATION TESTING
# ================================================================

maxTFCE <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = nperms,
  ncol = n_coef
)

colnames(maxTFCE) <- coef_names

cat("Starting permutation testing...\n")

for (p in seq_len(nperms)) {

  # Permute design matrix as in MATLAB
  XX <- X[
    rperms[, p],
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  perm_fit <- mass_ols(
    Y,
    XX
  )

  t_perm <- array(
    t(perm_fit$t),
    dim = c(
      n_chan,
      n_time,
      n_coef
    )
  )

  for (j in 2:n_coef) {

    tfce_perm <- tfce_2d(
      t_perm[, , j],
      adjacency = ChN,
      E = 0.66,
      H = 2,
      dh = 0.1
    )

    maxTFCE[p, j] <- max(
      abs(tfce_perm)
    )
  }

  if (p %% 100 == 0) {
    cat(
      "Permutation",
      p,
      "of",
      nperms,
      "\n"
    )
  }
}

cat("Permutation testing completed.\n")


# ================================================================
# STEP 9: FWER-CORRECTED P-VALUES
# ================================================================

alpha <- 0.05

Results <- list()

for (j in 2:n_coef) {

  observed <- tfce_obs[, , j]

  null_max <- maxTFCE[, j]

  p_values <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = n_chan,
    ncol = n_time
  )

  for (ch in seq_len(n_chan)) {

    for (tp in seq_len(n_time)) {

      p_values[ch, tp] <- (
        1 +
          sum(
            null_max >= abs(
              observed[ch, tp]
            )
          )
      ) / (nperms + 1)
    }
  }

  Results[[coef_names[j]]] <- list(
    Obs = observed,
    P_Values = p_values,
    Mask = p_values <= alpha
  )
}

cat("FWER-corrected inference completed.\n")


# ================================================================
# STEP 10: RASTER PLOT
# ================================================================

effect_name <- coef_names[2]

res <- Results[[effect_name]]

time_idx <- which(
  sEEG_times >= 0
)

plot_data <- expand.grid(
  Channel = seq_len(n_chan),
  Time = sEEG_times[time_idx]
)

plot_data$TFCE <- as.vector(
  res$Obs[, time_idx]
)

plot_data$Significant <- as.vector(
  res$Mask[, time_idx]
)

plot_data$TFCE_sig <- ifelse(
  plot_data$Significant,
  plot_data$TFCE,
  NA_real_
)

p_raster <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(
    x = Time,
    y = Channel
  )
) +
  geom_tile(
    aes(fill = TFCE_sig)
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "red",
    midpoint = 0,
    na.value = "grey85"
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(
    title = "TFCE-corrected EEG effects",
    x = "Time (ms)",
    y = "Channel",
    fill = "TFCE"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

print(p_raster)


# ================================================================
# STEP 11: TRACE PLOT
# ================================================================

# Replace with actual Fz, F3, F4, Cz indices
# after importing channel labels.

chm <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)

intercept <- betas[, , 1]
beta <- betas[, , 2]

trace_data <- data.frame(
  Time = rep(
    sEEG_times,
    3
  ),
  Value = c(
    colMeans(
      intercept[chm, , drop = FALSE]
    ),
    colMeans(
      beta[chm, , drop = FALSE]
    ),
    colMeans(
      intercept[chm, , drop = FALSE] +
        beta[chm, , drop = FALSE]
    )
  ),
  Effect = rep(
    c(
      "Intercept",
      "Condition B - A",
      "Condition B"
    ),
    each = n_time
  )
)

p_trace <- ggplot(
  trace_data,
  aes(
    x = Time,
    y = Value,
    color = Effect
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(-100, 1000)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated EEG coefficients",
    x = "Time (ms)",
    y = "Beta value (microvolts)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic()

print(p_trace)


# ================================================================
# STEP 12: SAVE RESULTS
# ================================================================

dir.create(
  "Results",
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  list(
    t_obs = t_obs,
    betas = betas,
    se = se,
    tfce_obs = tfce_obs,
    maxTFCE = maxTFCE,
    Results = Results,
    X = X,
    sEEG_times = sEEG_times
  ),
  file = "Results/lmeEEG_tutorialResult.rds"
)

ggsave(
  "Results/TFCE_raster.png",
  p_raster,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

ggsave(
  "Results/EEG_trace.png",
  p_trace,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

cat("lmeEEG analysis completed and saved.\n")

```
